# Canonical Calendar Data — Schema

**File:** `data/calendar/calendar-2026.json`
**Schema version:** `1.0`
**Introduced:** Update Track U1 (CHANGE-001 §4 "Full-Year Calendar JSON Data")
**Generated by:** `tools/generate-calendar.js` (deterministic; `--check` detects drift)

---

## 1. What this file represents

A **canonical, static, full-year calendar description for 2026**. It is the single source
for *calendar structure* and *study-cycle date metadata*: which days exist, what weekday
each one is, and what Study Planner cycle meaning belongs to each date.

It is deliberately **independent of the 28 generated daily-plan files** for ordinary
calendar structure — the year is fully described even for dates that have no study plan.

## 2. Top-level shape

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "1.0",
  "calendarType": "study-planner-canonical-calendar",
  "year": 2026,
  "generatedBy": "tools/generate-calendar.js",
  "sourceOfTruth": { "...": "..." },
  "studyCycle": {
    "startDate": "2026-10-02",
    "endDate": "2026-10-29",
    "totalDays": 28,
    "totalWeeks": 4,
    "studyWeekLength": 7,
    "startsOnWeekday": "Friday",
    "endsOnWeekday": "Thursday",
    "weeks": [{ "weekNumber": 1, "startDate": "...", "endDate": "...",
                "studyDayCount": 7 }],
    "gradedDates": ["2026-10-08", "..."],
    "practiceDates": ["2026-10-07", "..."]
  },
  "months": [{ "month": 1, "monthName": "January", "daysInMonth": 31,
               "dates": [ /* every date of the month, in order */ ] }]
}
```

`months[].dates` holds every date of that month in order. Across the year there are
exactly **365** date records (2026 is not a leap year).

## 3. Date record schema

Every date carries the same fields.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | string | ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. The one date identity in the app. |
| `year` / `month` / `day` | number | Calendar components (month is 1–12). |
| `monthName` | string | e.g. `"October"`. |
| `weekday` | string | Full name, e.g. `"Friday"`. |
| `weekdayShort` | string | `"Fri"` (matches the app's existing `WEEKDAY_SHORT`). |
| `weekdayIndex` | number | `0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday` (matches existing `calendar.js`). |
| `isoWeekday` | string | ISO-8601 name, e.g. `"Fri"`. |
| `isoWeekdayIndex` | number | ISO-8601 index: `0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday`. |
| `dayOfYear` | number | 1 … 365. |
| `isStudyCycleActive` | boolean | `true` only for the 28 cycle dates. |
| `studyWeek` | number \| null | 1–4 inside the cycle; **`null`** outside. |
| `studyDay` | number \| null | 1–7 **within** the study week; **`null`** outside. |
| `cycleDay` | number \| null | 1–28 across the whole cycle; **`null`** outside. |
| `isStudyWeekStart` | boolean | `studyDay === 1`. |
| `isStudyWeekEnd` | boolean | `studyDay === 7`. |
| `isGradedDay` | boolean | Derived from graded tasks in the plan. |
| `isPracticeDay` | boolean | Derived from practice tasks in the plan. |
| `special` | string \| null | `"graded"` \| `"practice"` \| `"study-week-start"` \| `null`. |
| `specialLabel` | string \| null | Display text for the special day. |
| `notes` | array | Always `[]` in U1 — placeholder for U2. |
| `events` | array | Always `[]` in U1 — placeholder for U2. |

### 3.1 `studyDay` vs `cycleDay` — do not confuse them

The generated daily plans store `dayNumber`, which is the **cycle** day (1–28 across the
whole cycle). The specification's "Study Day" is the day **within** the study week (1–7).

```text
studyDay = dayNumber - (weekNumber - 1) * 7
```

Both are exposed so no consumer has to derive one from the other:
`2026-10-09` is `cycleDay: 8`, `studyWeek: 2`, `studyDay: 1`.

### 3.2 `special` precedence

A date has at most one `special` value. When several apply, precedence is fixed and
deterministic:

```text
graded  >  practice  >  study-week-start  >  null
```

The booleans (`isGradedDay`, `isPracticeDay`, `isStudyWeekStart`) remain independent, so a
consumer can still test each condition separately.

## 4. Active vs inactive dates

Only the 28 dates covered by the generated cycle carry study metadata:

```json
// 2026-10-02  (cycle start)
{ "isStudyCycleActive": true, "studyWeek": 1, "studyDay": 1, "cycleDay": 1 }

// 2026-10-01  (before the cycle)
{ "isStudyCycleActive": false, "studyWeek": null, "studyDay": null,
  "cycleDay": null, "special": null, "specialLabel": null }
```

Inactive dates are ordinary calendar dates. They are **never** given fabricated study
metadata, and they still carry `notes: []` / `events: []`.

## 5. Graded-day metadata

Graded days are **derived from the authoritative plans**, not hardcoded: a date is graded
when its daily plan contains at least one task with `type === "graded"`. For the current
cycle these are `2026-10-08`, `2026-10-15`, `2026-10-22`, `2026-10-29` (each study day 7).
Future UI identifies a graded date by reading `isGradedDay` / `special` — never by
hardcoding "October 8 is graded".

## 6. Notes and events

Every date exposes `notes: []` and `events: []`. These are **empty placeholders** in U1.
U1 implements no note/event UI and never invents content. Future U2 work consumes these
arrays. Note that these are calendar-local annotations; they are unrelated to task
completion (which lives in `storage.js`).

## 7. Authority chain — what owns what

```text
Calendar structure ............ this canonical JSON file
Study-cycle meaning ........... data/schedule/daily/*.json, projected in by the generator
Planning ...................... src/js/planner-engine.js
Completion .................... src/js/storage.js
Progress ...................... src/js/progress-engine.js
Reports ....................... report-model / existing report architecture
```

- The **generator** reads the daily plans and projects their `weekNumber`, `dayNumber` and
  graded/practice meaning into the calendar. It never writes to them.
- The calendar file is **not** a second planner. It contains no lecture allocation,
  question counts, workload, capacity, or task distribution.
- The calendar file is **not** a progress engine and **not** a completion store. It holds
  no completion state.

## 8. What this file must NOT contain

- Runtime completion state (`completed`, `checked`, `isDone`, `percent`, …) — owned by
  `storage.js` / `progress-engine.js`.
- Syllabus content or a second copy of it — owned by `data/syllabus/` + `data-engine.js`.
- Task lists, allocations or any planning output — owned by `planner-engine.js`.
- Fabricated notes or events.

## 9. Regenerating and verifying

```bash
node tools/generate-calendar.js           # regenerate the file (deterministic)
node tools/generate-calendar.js --check   # fail if the file has drifted from a fresh build
```

Generation is deterministic: identical inputs always produce byte-identical output (no
clock reads, no randomness, stable key order). The generator **fails loudly** — exiting
non-zero — if the authoritative daily plans are inconsistent (missing study day, a week
that is not seven contiguous days, a cycle gap, a filename/date mismatch, or a cycle
boundary that does not match the declared start/end).

## 10. Consuming the data

`src/js/calendar.js` exposes `createCalendarAccess(doc)`, which indexes a parsed calendar
document and returns helpers (`getDate`, `getMonthDates`, `isActiveStudyDate`,
`getStudyMetadata`, `getStudyWeekDates`, `getGradedDates`, …). The document is passed in
by the caller; `calendar.js` never fetches by itself and never touches the DOM.

Note the deliberate distinction kept in `calendar.js`:

- `buildWeekDates(anchor)` — ordinary **Sunday→Saturday** calendar week. Unchanged; used
  for ordinary calendar display.
- `getStudyWeekDates(n)` — the canonical **Friday→Thursday** study week, read from this
  file. Used for Study Planner week navigation (future U2).
